title: Parameterized Testing
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of parameterized testing and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—testing multiple input combinations—in a small, readable example.
Identify one failure, compatibility, security, or resource-management concern and describe a safe response.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study parameterized testing with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you verify stated behavior with meaningful assertions, including edge and failure cases. In this lesson, focus on testing multiple input combinations and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat console input as untrusted text. Validate format and range before using it, account for token-versus-line reading, and give users a clear way to correct invalid input. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect testing multiple input combinations with parameterized test cases before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Testing multiple input combinations
items.text: Treat console input as untrusted text. Validate format and range before using it, account for token-versus-line reading, and give users a clear way to correct invalid input.

items.title: Parameterized test cases
items.text: A method gives a named contract to a unit of behavior. Keep responsibilities focused, define clear parameter and return types, and test typical, boundary, and invalid cases independently.

items.title: Reusing test logic
items.text: A good test states the behavior it verifies and isolates the cause of a failure. Include boundary and error cases; coverage alone does not prove that assertions are meaningful.

items.title: Keeping tests readable
items.text: A good test states the behavior it verifies and isolates the cause of a failure. Include boundary and error cases; coverage alone does not prove that assertions are meaningful.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Add assertions for normal, boundary, and invalid cases; this plain-Java example requires no external test framework. For ordinary Java SE examples, use JDK 25, save a complete class as Main.java, and run `javac Main.java` followed by `java Main`. CodeLeaf does not execute Java in the browser; use a local JDK for these examples. Preview-only and configuration-file examples have their own version or filename notes.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, remove any temporary output files it created, and rerun the baseline case. Do not leave credentials, generated private data, or large test files in the project directory.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.

content.task: Try it yourself: design a check for parameterized testing that includes a normal case, a boundary case, and a failure case. Make the check fail visibly when the behavior is wrong.

common_mistakes.problem: Applying the rule from memory without checking its exact contract.
common_mistakes.why: Small differences in type, scope, API version, or input shape can change the result.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the relevant official API/language documentation and build a minimal reproducer.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify the actual cause of a different result.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one factor at a time and keep a short record of observed behavior.

summary: Parameterized Testing is best understood by connecting its contract to a small observable example.
Key syllabus points: Testing multiple input combinations, Parameterized test cases, Reusing test logic.
Use official versioned documentation and tests to confirm assumptions before relying on behavior in a larger application.
